Sofia — quick read and suggested compromise language below. I kept it tight to reduce back-and-forth. Rationale and practical notes follow.

Suggested clause (Option 1 — preferred, narrow):
"Governing Law and Forum; Provisional Remedies. This Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to choice-of-law rules. The parties agree that any final adjudication of disputes arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in the State of Delaware. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek provisional, injunctive or conservatory relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo, prevent irreparable harm, or protect confidential information. The exercise of such provisional remedies shall not constitute a waiver of the right to have the dispute finally adjudicated in Delaware; provided that the party obtaining provisional relief shall (a) promptly notify the other party in writing, and (b) use commercially reasonable efforts to seek consolidation or transfer of the action to Delaware for final adjudication where feasible."

Alternative (Option 2 — carve to specific categories):
"Notwithstanding the exclusive forum clause, the parties may each seek provisional remedies in any court for the limited purposes of (i) preserving confidential or personal data, (ii) preserving intellectual property rights, and (iii) securing evidence at risk of destruction."

Practical notes:
- Option 1 is the cleanest: preserves Delaware as the single forum for final merits while giving both parties immediate local relief in emergencies.
- Add the notification + consolidation language to reduce prolonged parallel litigation. That is enforceable in many courts and signals intent.
- We should avoid language that expressly permits parallel merits litigation outside Delaware — keep the provisional relief limited to interim measures.
- If Acme insists on full carve (i.e., final injunctive adjudication outside Delaware), we should push back and offer expedited injunctive proceedings in Delaware as an alternative.

If everyone is comfortable, I can propose the Option 1 wording to Acme. If they accept, we can incorporate into the MSA and update the Order Form.

—Laura
General Counsel (Contracts & Commercial)
Redwood Inference
